_readme: EVERY piece of text on the site lives in this file. Edit it here, save, done —
you never need to open App.js. `npm start` hot-reloads your changes.
Rules, because JSON is picky:
- Wrap all text in "double quotes". Single quotes are not valid JSON.
- Put a comma between items, but NEVER after the last one in a list or block.
- A literal double quote inside text must be escaped: \"
- No comments allowed. This _readme block is the workaround; the site ignores it.
- Accents and symbols (é — · ≥) can be typed directly. The file is UTF-8.
Adding or removing an entry: copy an existing { ... } block, comma-separate it
from its neighbour, and edit the values. Order in the file = order on the page.
The three tiers of text under your name, largest to smallest:
1. `name`     — just your name.
2. `subtitle` — the one-line 'who I am'. Big and dark, reads as part of the name.
3. `bio`      — the paragraphs below the hairline. Smaller and softer.
Two things are NOT here, because search engines and link previews read them
before the page runs: the browser-tab title and the description that shows up
when you paste the URL into Slack/LinkedIn. Both are in public/index.html.
Images live in public/images/. A path of "/images/foo.jpg" means the file
public/images/foo.jpg. Project thumbnails render at roughly 380x238, so ship
them around 760x476 and 16:10 — anything else gets cropped from the centre.
name: Ihsan Salari
subtitle: UWaterloo EE student building AI systems informed by experience in signal integrity, datacenter optics, and RF for chip manufacturing.

bio._note: One string per paragraph. `fold` = how many paragraphs stay visible before the 'See more' button; the rest are hidden until it is clicked. Set fold to the number of paragraphs to disable the button entirely.
paragraphs: Ethics and social impact are far too often overlooked in engineering. These, along with environmental sustainability, are core to my work. With the advent of AI, it is increasingly important that we act with morality and worldly impact in mind.
Every role I've held has been in a domain I was new to, and every time I was owning critical deliverables within weeks.
At Arista, I worked on next-gen optics for AI (12.8T XPO, CPO/NPO, and 1.6T modules) and ensured signal integrity on PCIe Gen 5 and 224G links.
Currently, I'm at Fab2 (Atomic Semi), focusing on RF inverters and power systems for plasma generation within a chip manufacturing context.

theme._note: The light/dark toggle in the top-right. The label names where you are going, not where you are — it reads "Dark" while the site is light.

links._note: The row of links in the top-right corner. Add "download": true to save the file instead of opening it in a new tab.

experience._note: Click a row on the site to expand it. `when` is the small grey column on the left — give it one or two short pieces ("Summer" and "'26" stack on two lines). `org` and `role` are the always-visible lines. `points`, `tags` and `href` only appear once the row is expanded, and all three are optional: delete any you don't want.

ai._note: AI work, one row per project. Only the hidden preview path renders it for now (see README). `blurb` is the one sentence under the title; `meta` is the small grey tag line; `href` is where the row links. `docs` is optional: small links under the row, one { "label", "href" } per file; PDFs live in public/docs/, so "/docs/foo.pdf" means public/docs/foo.pdf. Delete it for a row with none. `link` is the one at the top-right of the section. Shelved rows (not on the site) are in content.shelved.json.
